title: The Hidden Words
author: Baha'u'llah
description: A short classic of Baha'i devotional literature, revealed by Baha'u'llah around 1857-58 while walking along the banks of the Tigris during his exile in Baghdad, and translated by Shoghi Effendi. It consists of seventy-one brief Arabic and eighty-two Persian aphorisms addressed by God to the human soul ('O Son of Spirit', 'O Son of Being'). Baha'u'llah presented it as the inner essence of what was revealed to the earlier Prophets, clothed in brevity. The verses teach love of God as the purpose of creation, detachment from the world, purity of heart, justice, humility, the transience of material life and the soul's return to its Source. Its poetic concision, comparable to Sufi wisdom sayings and the Psalms, has made it one of the most widely read and memorised Baha'i texts and an accessible doorway into the mystical ethics of the faith.
